cap: Two questions sort almost every genital ulcer: does the ulcer hurt, and what are the inguinal nodes doing? Herpes and chancroid ulcers are painful. The syphilis chancre, the fleeting ulcer of lymphogranuloma venereum and the beefy-red ulcer of donovanosis are painless. The node column then separates the look-alikes, from rubbery painless syphilitic nodes to the suppurating buboes of LGV and the pseudobuboes of donovanosis.
teach: Read across a row to build the whole picture of one infection, and down a column to compare. A painful ulcer with a suppurating node on one side is chancroid; painful grouped vesicles with fever are herpes. A painless ulcer with rubbery nodes is syphilis, a painless ulcer that bleeds easily is donovanosis, and painful buboes after an ulcer the patient barely noticed are lymphogranuloma venereum.
